content.user_title: Plan Trade Show Budgets and ROI
content.value_statement: Trade show teams need realistic cost estimates before they commit money. This skill builds itemized budgets, ROI projections, and approval-ready summaries for exhibition decisions.
actual_capabilities: Creates itemized budgets for booth space, travel, marketing, staffing, logistics, and operations.
Estimates exhibitor, attendee, and sponsor costs using provided details and benchmark assumptions.
Builds ROI projections with pipeline value, cost per lead, break-even deals, and sensitivity scenarios.
Suggests budget optimization options based on budget limits, event goals, and exhibitor experience.
Formats results as Markdown tables, CSV-ready content, or an executive summary for approval.
limitations: Cost estimates depend on user inputs, public rates, and benchmark assumptions.
The skill does not guarantee actual venue pricing, supplier quotes, or final ROI.
It needs current show details from the user or web research for precise budgets.
It does not replace finance, procurement, legal, or tax review.

use_cases.title: Estimate Exhibitor Costs
use_cases.description: Build a full booth budget with space, build, travel, marketing, staffing, and contingency costs.
use_cases.target_user: Marketing managers planning an exhibition booth

use_cases.title: Prepare Budget Approval
use_cases.description: Turn cost assumptions into an executive summary with ROI, break-even targets, and decision points.
use_cases.target_user: Sales leaders requesting event investment approval

use_cases.title: Compare Event Options
use_cases.description: Compare attending, exhibiting, and sponsoring across multiple events using consistent cost and ROI assumptions.
use_cases.target_user: Operations teams selecting trade show investments

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one show and simple inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a trade show budget for exhibiting at [show name] with a [booth size] booth and [team size] people. Include major cost categories and a contingency.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Attendee Costs
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan travel and attendance without a booth.
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate the cost for [team size] people to attend [show name] in [city]. Include registration, travel, hotel, meals, and staff time.

prompt_templates.title: Build an ROI Case
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an ROI case for exhibiting at [show name]. Our average deal value is [amount], expected leads are [number], and target conversion rate is [percent].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Strategic Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare attending, exhibiting, and sponsoring at [show name]. Use conservative, base, and optimistic ROI scenarios, then recommend the best option.

output_examples.input: How much would a 20 square meter booth at MEDICA cost for a four-person team?
output: An itemized exhibitor budget grouped by booth space, booth build, travel, marketing, staffing, logistics, and contingency.
A total investment estimate with notes showing which numbers are assumptions and which need vendor confirmation.
A short list of venue questions, including space rates, electrical costs, move-in timing, and mandatory services.

output_examples.input: Is it worth exhibiting if our average deal is 50,000 dollars?
output: A pipeline projection with expected visitors, qualified leads, opportunities, and closed deals.
Conservative, base, and optimistic ROI scenarios with cost per lead and break-even deal targets.
A recommendation that explains the financial case and the main risks behind the decision.

output_examples.input: Create a one-page budget summary for my manager.
output: An executive summary with total budget, main assumptions, expected outcomes, and approval considerations.
A concise explanation of cost drivers, ROI timing, and practical ways to reduce spend.

best_practices: Provide booth size, team size, event city, participation type, and business goals before asking for a budget.
Ask the skill to separate confirmed prices from estimated costs and benchmark assumptions.
Review conservative ROI scenarios before using the plan for leadership approval.
anti_patterns: Do not treat benchmark costs as final supplier quotes or venue invoices.
Do not omit contingency, logistics, internet, electrical, or staff opportunity costs.
Do not rely on optimistic lead conversion rates without evidence from prior events.

faq.question: Can this skill estimate booth costs for a specific trade show?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the show name, booth size, location, team size, and participation type for a detailed estimate.

faq.question: Can it create an ROI projection?
faq.answer: Yes. It can estimate leads, opportunities, revenue, ROI, cost per lead, and break-even deals.

faq.question: Does it use current venue prices automatically?
faq.answer: Only when current information is supplied or researched. Otherwise, it labels numbers as estimates or benchmark assumptions.

faq.question: Can it compare exhibiting with attending only?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare participation models and explain cost, reach, and ROI tradeoffs.

faq.question: What formats can it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce Markdown tables, CSV-ready budget lines, and executive summaries for approval reviews.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
